q: 201. When a reinforced concrete structure is loaded, the resistance first broken is
explain: The bond between steel and concrete is composed of adhesion, friction, and mechanical interlock. Adhesive resistance (the chemical bond) is the first to fail as soon as there is any microscopic slip.

q: 202. As per IS 456 : 1978, the permissible value of bond stress for M15 grade if concrete is limited to
explain: According to the older IS 456:1978 code (Working Stress Method), the permissible design bond stress for M15 concrete using plain bars in tension is 1.0 N/mm².

q: 203. If the bond stress developed in a reinforced concrete beam is more than permissible value, it can be brought down by
options: decreasing the diameter of the bars
explain: Bond stress depends on the total perimeter of the bars. By increasing the number of bars or decreasing the diameter (while maintaining area), the total surface area increases, which reduces bond stress. Increasing depth also reduces the force required, thus reducing bond stress.

q: 204. If φ is the diameter of reinforcing bar, then for M15 grade concrete, the bond length used for splicing bar in tension is approximately equal to
explain: For M15 grade and plain bars, the development length (Ld) is roughly 58φ. Splicing requirements in tension are usually equal to the development length or slightly more depending on the specific code version.

q: 205. For reinforcing bars in compression, the average bond stress can be increased by
explain: IS 456 specifies that design bond stress values for bars in tension shall be increased by 25% for bars in compression, as the compression tends to expand the bar and tighten the grip.

q: 206. In the case of deformed bars, the value of bond stress for various grades of concrete is greater by... than the plain bars.
explain: Deformed bars (like HYSD) provide better mechanical interlock than plain bars. Codes allow a 60% increase in design bond stress for deformed bars.

q: 207. When the diameter of a reinforcement bar is φ, the anchorage value of the hook alone is equal to
explain: A standard U-type hook provides an anchorage value equivalent to a straight length of 16 times the diameter (16φ) of the bar.

q: 208. The length of lab for reinforcement bars in compression shall not be less than
explain: For bars in compression, the lap length is usually the development length in compression (φσs / 4τbd) but must not be less than 24φ.

q: 209. The maximum spacing of vertical reinforcement in R.C.C. wall should not exceed the thickness of wall
explain: As per standard practice for reinforced concrete walls, the spacing of vertical reinforcement should not exceed 3 times the wall thickness or 450mm, whichever is smaller.

q: 210. In a doubly reinforced beam, steel reinforcement is provided in a
explain: A doubly reinforced beam contains longitudinal reinforcement in both the tension and the compression zones to increase the moment capacity when dimensions are restricted.

q: 211. A doubly reinforced section in used
options: when the members are subjected to alternate external loads and the bending moment in the sections reverses
when the members are subjected to loading eccentric on either side of the axis
explain: Doubly reinforced sections are ideal for situations where moments reverse (like in seismic loading) or where the concrete alone cannot handle the compression due to eccentricity or restricted size.

q: 212. A doubly reinforced beam is considered less economical than a singly reinforced beam because
options: tensile steel requires is more than that for balanced section
concrete is not stressed to its full value
explain: In a doubly reinforced beam, the stress in the compression steel is limited by the strain in the surrounding concrete. Often, it does not reach its full yield strength, making the use of steel less efficient than in the tension zone.

q: 213. If the area of tensile steel reinforcement is doubled, the moment of resistance of the beam increases only by about
explain: Doubling the steel area shifts the neutral axis downward, reducing the lever arm and causing the concrete to reach its capacity faster. This leads to a non-proportional increase in moment capacity, roughly around 22%.

q: 214. In the steel beam theory of doubly reinforced concrete beams, it is assumed that
options: stress in compression steel is equal to stress in tension steel
in tension and compression concrete, no stress in developed
explain: Steel beam theory is a simplified method that assumes concrete provides no resistance at all, and the tension/compression are handled entirely by the steel at equal stress levels.

q: 215. The concrete below the neutral axis
explain: In reinforced concrete design, concrete in the tension zone (below the neutral axis) is assumed to be cracked and contributes nothing to bending resistance; its primary role is to provide cover and bond (embedment) for the steel.

q: 216. The section of the beam having greater width at the top in comparison to the width below neutral axis is known as
explain: A T-beam consists of a wide top flange (which handles compression) and a narrow rib below (the web), resulting in a wider top than bottom.

q: 217. The breadth of rib in a T-beam should at least be equal to... the depth of rib.
explain: For structural stability and to avoid lateral buckling of the web, the breadth of the rib is generally recommended to be at least 1/3 of the depth of the rib.

q: 218. In a T-beam, the vertical distance between the bottom of the flange and the centre of the tensile reinforcement is known as the
explain: The 'rib' or 'web' is the portion of the beam below the flange. The vertical distance from the underside of the flange to the reinforcement level is essentially the depth of the rib.

q: 219. The side face reinforcement, if required, in a T-beam will be
options: 0.2 % to 0.3 % of the web area depending upon the breadth of the slab
explain: When the depth of the web exceeds 750 mm, side face reinforcement is provided at 0.1% of the web area, distributed equally on both faces.

q: 220. The assumed overall depth of the T-beam is taken as... of the span when it is supported t ends.
explain: For initial trial sizing of a simply supported T-beam, the overall depth is generally assumed to be between 1/12 and 1/15 of the span.

q: 221. When the T-beam is continuous, the assumed overall depth of the beam of heavy loads is taken as
explain: Continuous beams under heavy loads require higher stiffness, leading to a depth assumption closer to 1/10 to 1/12 of the span.

q: 222. The neutral axis in T-beam section falls
explain: Depending on the reinforcement area and flange dimensions, the neutral axis can either lie within the slab (flange) or extend down into the rib.

q: 223. A T-beam behaves like a rectangular beam of width equal to its flange, if neutral axis
explain: When the neutral axis is within the flange, the entire compression zone is rectangular (width = Bf). Since concrete in tension is ignored, the shape of the web doesn't affect the stress calculation.

q: 224. In a reinforced concrete T-beam (in which the flange is in compression), the position of neutral axis will
options: depend on the thickness of flange is in relation to total depth and percentage of reinforcement
at the junction of flange and web
explain: The position of the neutral axis is determined by the equilibrium of total compression and total tension, which depends on the steel ratio and the geometry of the section.

q: 225. The width of the flange of T-beam should be less than
options: one-third of the effective span of the T-beam
distance between the centres of T-beam
breadth of the rib plus twelve times the thickness of the slab
prev_options: This corresponds to the code limitations for effective width of flange.
explain: The effective width of a T-beam flange is limited to the minimum of several factors (span/6 + bw + 6df, or center-to-center distance) to account for shear lag.

q: 226. The width of the flange of L-beam, should be less than
options: breadth of the rib + four times thickness of the slab
breadth of the rib + half clear distance between ribs
explain: Similar to T-beams, L-beams have specific geometric limits in the code for 'effective width'—usually based on span, rib width, and slab thickness.

q: 227. Thought the effective depth of a T-beam is the distance between the top compression edge to centre of the tensile reinforcement, for heavy loads, it is taken as
explain: For heavy loading conditions in flanged beams, a stiffer section is required, typically leading to an effective depth around 1/12 of the span.

q: 228. For the design of a simply supported T-beam the ratio of the effective span to the overall depth the beam is limited to
explain: For span/depth ratios regarding deflection control (IS 456), the value for a simply supported beam is generally taken as 20.

q: 229. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: at the bottom edge of the slab
explain: If the compression zone (neutral axis) is contained entirely within the top flange, the calculation is identical to that of a rectangular beam of flange width.

q: 230. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: coincides the geometrical centre of the beam
explain: This is a repetition of the principle in Q229; as long as the NA is in the flange, it behaves as a rectangular beam.

q: 231. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. cantilever members is placed at
explain: In a cantilever beam, tension occurs at the top because it bends downward (hogging moment). Therefore, main reinforcement must be at the top.

q: 232. The main reinforcement in R.C.C simply supported member is placed at
explain: A simply supported beam under gravity loads experiences sagging (tension at the bottom), so reinforcement is placed in the bottom fibre.

q: 233. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. continuous members is placed at
explain: Continuous beams experience sagging (bottom tension) in the span and hogging (top tension) at the supports, requiring reinforcement at both top and bottom.

q: 234. An additional longitudinal reinforcement in webs of beams should be placed if the depth of the web is more than 750 mm at
explain: Side face reinforcement is required in deep beams (web > 750mm) to control cracking due to shrinkage and temperature.

q: 235. The maximum strain in the tension reinforcement at failure shall not be less than
explain: Per Limit State Method (IS 456), the minimum strain in steel at failure to ensure ductility is (0.87fy / Es) + 0.002. Note: 0.87 is 1/1.15.

q: 236. The ratio of the compressive strength of concrete is structure to the characteristic strength of concrete in cube is equal to
explain: Because of size and shape differences between a test cube and the actual structure, the design compressive strength of concrete in the structure is taken as 0.67 times the cube strength (fck).

q: 237. The shape of the stress-strain curve for compression in concrete is generally taken to be
explain: In the Limit State Method, the stress-strain block is usually assumed to be parabolic up to a strain of 0.002 and rectangular thereafter.

q: 238. The partial factor of safety for steel in limit state design is
explain: The partial safety factor for steel (γs) is 1.15 because steel is a factory-manufactured material with better quality control than concrete.

q: 239. The partial factor of safety for concrete in limit state design is
explain: The partial safety factor for concrete (γc) is 1.50, reflecting higher uncertainty in site-mixed concrete compared to steel.

q: 240. The maximum allowable percentage of tension reinforcement in R.C.C. beams is
explain: To prevent congestion and ensure proper concrete placement, IS 456 limits the maximum area of tension reinforcement to 4% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 241. A continuous beam shall be deemed to be a deep beam if the ratio of effective span to overall depth, is
explain: According to IS 456, a beam is considered deep when the L/D ratio is less than 2.0 for a simply supported beam and less than 2.5 for a continuous beam.

q: 242. The maximum area of tension reinforcement in beams shall not exceed
explain: Same as Q240; the limit is 4% of the gross area (bD).

q: 243. Side face reinforcement shall be provided in the beam when depth of the web in a beam exceeds
explain: If the web depth exceeds 75 cm (750 mm), side face reinforcement must be provided.

q: 244. A reinforced concrete beam is design to resist
explain: A complete beam design must account for flexural tension (steel), flexural compression (concrete/steel), and shear (stirrups).

q: 245. Concrete is fairly strong in
options: tension but very weak in compression
compression but very weak in tension
explain: Concrete is a brittle material that performs well under compression but has very little tensile strength (roughly 1/10th of its compressive strength).

q: 246. Steel is very strong
explain: While steel can handle both, its primary purpose in RCC is its high tensile strength to compensate for concrete's weakness.

q: 247. In singly reinforced simply supported beams, the reinforced steel bars are placed
options: near the bottom of the beam
near the top of the beam
at the neutral axis of the beam
anywhere in the cross section of the beam
explain: In a simply supported beam, the bottom fiber is in tension, so the reinforcement must be placed there.

q: 248. A reinforced concrete beam subjected to a monotonously increasing load may fail at
explain: A beam design ensures that it only fails when it reaches its ultimate capacity (Ultimate Strength Stage).

q: 249. The simple bending equation is applicable to a reinforced concrete beam subjected to a monotonously increasing load when the beam remains in
explain: Simple bending theory (linear elastic) applies best when the section is homogenous and uncracked. Once cracks appear, the section properties change significantly.

q: 250. At cracked concrete stage of a reinforced concrete beam, the maximum tensile stress in concrete remains
options: less than its modulus of rupture
more than its modulus of rupture
explain: Concrete cracks once the tensile stress exceeds its Modulus of Rupture (flexural tensile strength).

q: 251. The analysis and design of reinforced concrete beam at the cracked concrete stage is done by
explain: The Working Stress Method (WSM) is based on the elastic theory and assumes the concrete is cracked and the steel carries all tension, focusing on serviceability at the cracked stage.

q: 252. The ratio of the depth of the parabolic and rectangular portion block at the limit state of collapse of a singly reinforced section is
explain: In the IS 456 stress block, the rectangular portion is 3/7th and the parabolic portion is 4/7th of the neutral axis depth. The ratio 4/7 : 3/7 is 4:3.

q: 253. The distance between the lines of action of compression and tensile forces in a singly reinforced beam is called
explain: The lever arm (z) is the internal distance between the resultant compressive force (C) in concrete and the resultant tensile force (T) in steel.

q: 254. If the ratio of steel to concrete in a beam is such that maximum strain in both materials reach simultaneously, the beam is referred to as
explain: A balanced section is a theoretical design where the concrete reaches its maximum allowable compressive strain at the exact same time the steel reaches its yield strain.

q: 255. Compression failure of simply reinforced beam occurs in
explain: In an over-reinforced beam, the concrete reaches its crushing strain before the steel yields, leading to a sudden, brittle compression failure.

q: 256. Tension failure occurs is singly reinforced beam in
explain: In an under-reinforced beam, the steel yields first. This provides ample warning (cracking and deflection) before the concrete eventually crushes, termed a tension failure.

q: 257. Yielding of steel in singly reinforced beam occurs in
explain: Yielding of steel is the defining characteristic of an under-reinforced section, ensuring a ductile failure mode.

q: 258. The ratio of the limiting value of the depth of neutral axis and the depth of the section of a singly reinforced beam is equal to
explain: This formula is derived from the linear strain diagram where the maximum concrete strain is 0.0035 and the minimum steel strain is 0.002 + 0.87fy/Es.

q: 259. The limiting moment of resistance for a singly reinforced beam using Fe 250 steel and general grade concrete, is
explain: For Fe 250 steel (mild steel), the limiting moment of resistance factor (Mu,lim) is 0.148 (rounded to 0.149 in some texts) times fck·bd².

q: 260. The most economical design of singly reinforced beams is given by
explain: Limit State Method (LSM) is more economical as it uses partial safety factors and accounts for the non-linear behavior of concrete, allowing for smaller sections than WSM.

q: 261. The aspect ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: length to breadth of a slab
effective width of flange and effective depth of the beam
width of web and depth of flange
explain: Aspect ratio (ly/lx) is the ratio of the longer span to the shorter span of a slab, used to determine if it is one-way or two-way.

q: 262. The dowel force is the shear force
options: at the top of the beam
at the bottom of the beam
explain: Dowel action refers to the ability of longitudinal reinforcement bars to transfer shear forces across a crack.

q: 263. To ensure that under the applied moment the concrete and steel in singly reinforced beam reach their stresses, the minimum area of steel
explain: As per IS 456, the minimum tension reinforcement (As) is given by As/bd = 0.85/fy.

q: 264. For a rectangular simply supported beam for 4.5 m effective span, based on the code restriction, the depth is
explain: For a simply supported beam, span/depth = 20. Thus, Depth = 4500 / 20 = 225 mm.

q: 265. The strain at the level of compression reinforcement is doubly reinforced beam is
explain: From the strain triangle, the strain at depth d' is linearly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis: εsc = 0.0035 * (xu - d') / xu.

q: 266. In doubly reinforced beams, the percentage of the maximum compression reinforcement of the gross cross-sectional area of beam should not exceed
explain: Similar to tension reinforcement, compression reinforcement is also capped at 4% of the gross area to prevent congestion.

q: 267. The slab forming the top part of flanged the beam mid span in subject to compression over a length
options: greater than the width of the rib
equal to the width of the rib
less than the width of the rib
equal to the perimeter of effective rectangular of the section
explain: In flanged beams (T-beams), a portion of the slab (the flange) acts with the rib to resist compression, making the compression width much larger than the rib width.

q: 268. At continuous supports, the lower portion of
options: the slab experience neither the tension nor compression
explain: At supports of a continuous beam, hogging occurs. This means the top is in tension and the bottom (lower portion) is in compression.

q: 269. The intermediate beams between several beams case monolithically with the slab
explain: Beams cast monolithically with a slab act as T-beams when they have slabs on both sides (intermediate) and L-beams on the ends.

q: 270. For simply supported beams of spans above 10 m, span to depth ratio 20 must be multiplied to get permitted value by
explain: For spans exceeding 10m, the span-to-depth ratios are modified by multiplying by (10 / span in meters).

q: 271. When strains in compression zone of the concrete of a loaded singly reinforced beam, cause crushing of concrete, the failure is known as
explain: Primary compression failure occurs in over-reinforced sections where concrete reaches its limit before the steel yields.

q: 272. The capacity of beam is determined by the load which causes
explain: In standard under-reinforced design, the beam's capacity is reached when the steel yields (ultimate limit state).

q: 273. For design purpose of flexural members, the compressive strength of concrete is assumed to be
explain: Design strength = (0.67 * fck) / 1.5 (Partial Safety Factor) ≈ 0.446 fck, often simplified or rounded to 0.42-0.45 in various literature batches.

q: 274. For the design of flexural members, the safety partial fact for compressive strength
explain: The partial safety factor for concrete (γc) is 1.5.

q: 275. For the design purpose of flexural members, the partial safety factor for stress in the reinforcement
explain: The partial safety factor for steel (γs) is 1.15.

q: 276. A double reinforced beam may be provided from
explain: Doubly reinforced beams are used when depth is limited (headroom/architecture) or to increase ductility and resist reversal of moments (structural).

q: 277. Thickness of slab is taken
explain: While slab thickness varies, in the context of flanged beam design trials, df is often taken around 0.25d or the actual slab thickness.

q: 278. When the ratio of the long to short dimensions of the slab in greater than X, the slab may be designed as one-way slab where X is
explain: If Ly/Lx > 2.0, the slab primarily bends in the shorter direction and is designed as a one-way slab.

q: 279. The minimum percentage of high yield strength deformed reinforcement bars (H.Y.S.D.) provided in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: For HYSD bars, the minimum reinforcement is 0.12% of the gross area. (For mild steel, it is 0.15%).

q: 280. The maximum diameter of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum diameter of reinforcing bars shall not exceed 1/8th of the total thickness of the slab.

q: 281. The maximum diameter of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. beams is limited to
options: one-eighth of the least dimension of the beams
one-tenth of the depth of beams
explain: General detailing guidelines suggest bar diameter should not exceed 1/8th of the least dimension to ensure bond and concrete flow.

q: 282. The maximum spacing of the torsional reinforcement in R.C.C. beams must not exceed
explain: Torsional stirrups must be closely spaced; the limit is the least of x1, (x1+y1)/4, or 300mm.

q: 283. The minimum number of torsional longitudinal reinforcement bars to be provided in R.C.C. beams is
explain: At least one longitudinal bar must be placed in each corner of the stirrups to resist torsion, total of 4 bars.

q: 284. The probability that the actual strengths of material is more than or equal to its characteristic strength is
explain: Characteristic strength is defined as the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall, meaning 95% are above it.

q: 285. The analysis of slab spanning is one direction is done by assuming it to be a beam of
explain: One-way slabs are designed as a series of 1-meter wide rectangular beams.

q: 286. The purpose of transverse reinforcement, in a slab, is to
options: distribute the effects of point load on the slab more evenly and uniformly
distribute the shrinkage and temperature cracks more evenly
keep the main reinforcement is position
explain: Transverse (distribution) steel handles temperature changes, shrinkage, and aids in load distribution.

q: 287. In a slab, the transverse reinforcement is provided at... to the span of the slab
explain: Transverse reinforcement is placed perpendicular (90 degrees) to the main span reinforcement.

q: 288. For bridge slabs, the amount of transverse reinforcement is taken as
explain: Specific codes for bridges often require higher distribution steel, typically 0.3% of the gross area.

q: 289. For simply supported slabs spanning in one direction, the ratio of span to overall depth should exceed
explain: For slabs, the span/overall depth ratio is typically kept around 25-30 for simply supported spans to control deflection.

q: 290. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the deflection of reinforced concrete slab or beam, for the purpose of design, is limited to... of span
explain: The span/250 limit is equivalent to 0.4%, but the question refers to the 1978 version where specific limits for finishes were set at 0.25% (span/400).

q: 291. A reinforced concrete slab is 75 mm thick. The maximum size of reinforcement bar that can be used is
explain: Max diameter = Thickness / 8 = 75 / 8 = 9.375 mm. The standard bar size below this is 8 mm.

q: 292. The shrinkage in a concrete slab
explain: As concrete dries, it shrinks. If restrained, this shrinkage develops internal tensile stresses, leading to tension cracks.

q: 293. The diameter of bars for main reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Main bars in slabs are typically between 8mm and 14mm. Bars smaller than 8mm are usually only used for distribution.

q: 294. The diameter of bars used for distribution reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Distribution or temperature bars are typically smaller, ranging from 6mm to 8mm.

q: 295. In a simply supported slab, alternate bars are curtailed at
explain: In simply supported slabs, bending moment reduces towards the ends, so bars are often cranked or curtailed at L/7 from the center of the support.

q: 296. According to Grashoff-Rankine theory, for a two-way slab which of the following holds true
explain: The theory states that load distribution is proportional to the inverse of the spans to the 4th power.

q: 297. For a slab spanning in two directions, the ratio of span to the depth of slab should not exceed
explain: For two-way slabs simply supported, the span/depth ratio limit is 35 (using Fe 250) or 28 (using Fe 415).

q: 298. In case of two-way slab, the limiting deflection of the slab is
options: primarily a function of the long span
primarily a function of the short span
independent of long or short spans
dependent on both long and short spans
explain: Deflection control for two-way slabs is based on the shorter span because it is the stiffer direction that carries more load.

q: 299. If the sides of a slab simply supported on its edges and spanning in two ways are equal, then the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab, the load is shared equally, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way span of the same length.

q: 300. The drop are provided in flat slabs to resist
explain: Drops (thickened portions of the slab) are primarily provided to increase the slab's resistance to punching shear at the column connection.
